accepted.s: The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM), maintained under ISRO’s Disaster Management Support Programme, is best described as a:
o: National register of disaster-related court cases
Satellite-based system exclusively for cyclone prediction
Communication network used only by the armed forces
GIS repository covering the entire disaster management cycle
accepted.x: NDEM is a GIS repository intended to support the whole disaster management cycle, from preparedness to recovery.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact institutional function rather than choosing a broader but incorrect description.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Google Earth Engine is particularly useful in disaster management because it:
o: Processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping
Operates India’s network of cyclone shelters
Issues statutory evacuation orders to district authorities
accepted.x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.
accepted.tq: Match the technology with its specific operational use.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding hazard zonation:
1. Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous zones.
2. Such zoning is based on the degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk.
3. Hazard-zonation maps are deterministic declarations that a disaster will certainly occur at a particular location.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hazard-zonation maps are probabilistic; they do not guarantee that a disaster will occur at a particular location.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme interpretation that converts a probabilistic map into a certainty.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Bhukosh portal of the Geological Survey of India hosts landslide-susceptibility maps covering approximately:
accepted.x: GSI’s Bhukosh portal hosts landslide-susceptibility maps covering about 4.3 lakh square kilometres.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive numerical coverage figure.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The landslide-susceptibility maps hosted on GSI’s Bhukosh portal are mirrored to the GIS portal of the:
accepted.x: The maps are mirrored to the NDMA GIS portal through web map services.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-link trap by distinguishing the mapping agency from the receiving agency.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) in disaster management?
o: It classifies geological hazards according to magnitude
It divides a district into seismic microzones
It estimates the financial loss after a disaster
accepted.x: CAP is used to integrate and disseminate public warnings through compatible alerting systems.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of an official technical term.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.x: The Lightning Detection System covers 104 locations.

accepted.s: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR are used in disaster management primarily to:
accepted.x: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR provide satellite-based support for cyclone tracking.
accepted.tq: Associate the named satellites with their distinctive disaster-management application.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered among the hazards supported by ISRO’s Disaster Management Support Programme?
accepted.x: The programme supports management of floods, cyclones, droughts, forest fires, landslides and earthquakes; election-related violence is not listed.
accepted.tq: Find the odd item outside the stated hazard group.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is included in the research and development activities of ISRO’s Disaster Management Support Programme?
1. Cyclone track and landfall studies
2. Earthquake precursors
3. Coastal vulnerability assessment
4. Landslide warning
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four activities—cyclone track and landfall, earthquake precursors, coastal vulnerability and landslide warning—are included.
accepted.tq: When all listed functions belong to one programme, use the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: ■ Technology in DM - GIS, remote sensing, flood mapping, hazard zonation  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An earthquake occurring in an uninhabited desert, without causing damage to people or property, is best classified as a:
accepted.x: A hazard is a potentially damaging event. It becomes a disaster when it interacts with a vulnerable population or exposed assets.
accepted.tq: Apply the hazard–disaster distinction to a concrete situation.
accepted.sec: ■ Hazard vs disaster vs vulnerability vs risk  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which expression best represents the relationship between hazard, vulnerability and disaster?
accepted.x: A disaster results when a hazard meets a vulnerable population; this relationship is expressed as Hazard × Vulnerability = Disaster.
accepted.tq: Recall the conceptual formula and distinguish multiplication from addition or subtraction.
accepted.sec: ■ Hazard vs disaster vs vulnerability vs risk  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Risk in disaster management generally rises with hazard, exposure and vulnerability, but falls with:
accepted.x: Risk increases with hazard, exposure and vulnerability, while stronger coping capacity reduces it.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of relationships rather than merely recalling the definition.
accepted.sec: ■ Hazard vs disaster vs vulnerability vs risk  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a community vulnerability factor?
accepted.x: Kutcha housing, weak health infrastructure and weak early warning increase vulnerability. High crop-insurance coverage tends to reduce vulnerability.
accepted.tq: Reverse the vulnerability indicators and identify the protective condition.
accepted.sec: ■ Hazard vs disaster vs vulnerability vs risk  [APPSC]

accepted.s:

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) functions under the framework of the:
o: National Security Act, 1980 and Andhra Pradesh Police Rules, 2007
Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 and Andhra Pradesh Health Rules, 2007
Environment Protection Act, 1986 and Andhra Pradesh Forest Rules, 2007
Disaster Management Act, 2005 and Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules, 2007
accepted.x: APSDMA was constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and operates in accordance with the Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules, 2007.
accepted.tq: Match the authority with its governing statute and rules.
accepted.sec: ■ APSDMA - statutory functions and cyclone cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following functions falls within the mandate of APSDMA?
1. Running the State Emergency Operations Centre
2. Coordinating with districts
3. Operating early-warning systems
4. Planning post-disaster restoration
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates districts, operates early warnings and undertakes pre-disaster planning and post-disaster restoration.
accepted.tq: Group statutory functions across preparedness, response and recovery phases.
accepted.sec: ■ APSDMA - statutory functions and cyclone cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only measures used in cyclone risk reduction in Andhra Pradesh?
o: IMD warnings, cyclone shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangroves
Deep mining, dam demolition, desalination and river diversion
Only post-cyclone compensation and crop harvesting
Forest clearance, coastal construction and removal of mangroves
accepted.x: Cyclone risk reduction measures include IMD warnings, shelters, evacuation, shelter belts and mangrove protection or restoration.
accepted.tq: Select the complete set of coordinated mitigation and preparedness measures.
accepted.sec: ■ APSDMA - statutory functions and cyclone cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s:

accepted.s: The change in Andhra Pradesh’s disaster-management approach is described as a shift from:
o: A mitigation-centric approach to a relief-centric approach
A district-centric approach to a village-centric approach only
A warning-based approach to a compensation-only approach
A relief-centric approach to a mitigation-centric approach
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has moved from a relief-centric approach towards a mitigation-centric approach and is regarded as a national leader in disaster-risk reduction.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of institutional change; reversed comparisons are a common trap.
accepted.sec: ■ APSDMA - statutory functions and cyclone cases  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is correct?
o: It is a force recruited solely from state police departments.
It is a scientific body concerned only with satellite imaging.
It is composed exclusively of elected representatives of affected districts.
It is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces and includes search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads.
accepted.x: NDRF is a specialist force drawn from central paramilitary forces, with search-and-rescue teams, engineers and dog squads, functioning under the superintendence of NDMA.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the force’s composition and specialist capabilities precisely.
accepted.sec: ■ NDRF - battalions, mock exercises, named exercises  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The NDRF functions under the superintendence of the:
o: State Disaster Management Authority of the affected state
accepted.x: The NDRF operates under the superintendence of the National Disaster Management Authority.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who supervises this body?’ institutional-authority test.
accepted.sec: ■ NDRF - battalions, mock exercises, named exercises  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A major institutional gap that can strain the NDRF during simultaneous disasters is that:
o: State Disaster Response Forces are not yet set up in all states
State authorities are prohibited from conducting disaster exercises
The NDRF has no search-and-rescue teams
The NDRF is not linked with any central authority
accepted.x: SDRFs have not yet been established in all states, increasing pressure on the NDRF when several disasters occur simultaneously.
accepted.tq: Identify the capacity gap that explains the operational consequence.
accepted.sec: ■ NDRF - battalions, mock exercises, named exercises  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following has been suggested to address the strain on NDRF during simultaneous disasters?
1. Mandatory establishment of SDRFs
2. Joint NDRF–SDRF training
3. Exclusive dependence on foreign rescue forces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The suggested measures are mandatory SDRFs and joint NDRF–SDRF training. Exclusive dependence on foreign rescue forces is not proposed.
accepted.tq: Separate the two valid institutional reforms from the exaggerated distractor.
accepted.sec: ■ NDRF - battalions, mock exercises, named exercises  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
